full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary to dispose this petition are that the petitioner as the plaintiff tiled Other Suit No.346 of 2012 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3r Court, Chittagong for specific performance of contract impleading the respondents as the defendants stating, inter alia, that defendant No.1 (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) entered into an agreement for sale of the suit land with the plaintiff for a consideration of Taka 1, 00, 00,000 (one crore) and on receipt of Taka. 50, 00,000 (fifty lac) as earnest money on 26-5-2009, he executed two registered Bainapatra bearing Nos.7930 and 7831 and handed over the possession of the suit land to him (the plaintiff) by executing a separate deed and also handed over the relevant papers regarding the suit land. It was stipulated in the Bainapatra that the plaintiff would make payment of the balance consideration money of Taka 50,00,000 (fifty lac) to the defendant within one year and then he would execute and register the sale deed. The plaintiff spent Taka 30,00,000 (thirty lac) in repairing the two and half storied building and setting up machineries worth Taka 4,00,00,000 (four crore) and he has been running his business in the suit land, As the suit land was not mutated in the name of the defendant and there was problem in obtaining permission from defendant No.2 to sell the suit land, the defendant could not execute and register the sale deed pursuant to the agreement dated 26-5-2009, the plaintiff proposed to the defendant to renew the Bainanama to which the defendant agreed with a condition to pay him the balance consideration of Taka 50,00,000 (fifty lac) and the plaintiff agreed to the same and accordingly on 25-5-2011, the defendant executed and registered the renewal Bainanpatra stipulating that the sale deed would be executed and registered within one year by mutating his name and obtaining permission of sale from defendant No.2. As per the stipulation of the Bainapatra dated 26-5-2009, the plaintiff paid off the balance consideration of Taka 50,00,000 (fifty lacs) to the defendant, but the payment of the said amount was not mentioned as the defendant stated that, if the said amount was mentioned in the Bainapatra, the registration fee would be the same as that of a saf kabala. The defendant on 25-5-2011 executed a mutual agreement and in clause 7 of Bainapatra No.7830, it was clearly stated that the balance amount of the Bainapatra would not be required to be paid at the time of execution of the Bainapatra. The defendant received the balance consideration money of Taka 50,00,000 (fifty lac) on several dates and there was no outstanding of the price of the suit land. The plaintiff requested the defendant on several occasions to execute and register the sale deed but the defendant killed time by dilly-dally tactics and lastly on 21-5-2015 refused to execute and register the kabala in terms of agreement; hence the plaintiff instituted the suit. 

 3. In the suit, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 appeared and filed separate sets of written statement. Thereafter, they filed two separate applications under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaintiffs suit was not maintainable, as he filed the suit without making the necessary deposit as mandated by section 21 A of the Specific Relief Act. 

 4. The trial Court by its order dated 21-8-2014 rejected the plaint on the ground of non deposit of the balance amount as per terms of the deed of agreement dated 25-5-2011. Rejection of plaint being a decree within the meaning of section 2(2) of the Code, the plaintiff filed the above mentioned first appeal before the High Court Division. The High Court Division dismissed the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree; hence this petition for leave to appeal. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Haque, learned Advocate for the petitioner drawing our attention to the statements made in the plaint particularly paragraph 7 thereof submits that in the said paragraph, it was categorically stated that plaintiffs made the entire payment of the value of the suit land as per terms of the agreement and there was no outstanding of the price as per terms of the agreement, there was no scope and need to deposit the balance consideration money at the time of filing the suit pursuant to the provisions of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act. But the trial Court as well as the High Court Division failed to consider the said averment made in the plaint and thereby erred in law in rejecting the plaint. He has further submitted that the High Court Division was wrong in holding that receipt showing payment of the balance amount pursuant to the agreement was compulsorily registrable under the provisions of section 17(1)(c) of the Registration Act and since "The receipt as produced having not been registered, we find that the learned Judge committed no illegality in rejecting the plaint, " and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree calls for interference by this Court. 

 6. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Advocate who entered caveat on behalf of the defendant-respondent, on the other hand, has supported the judgment and decree of the High Court Division submitting that the registration of the receipt showing payment of the balance consideration pursuant to the agreement for sale being compulsory, the unregistered money receipt produced by the plaintiff showing payment of the balance consideration money was not prima-facie acceptable, and the balance amount of consideration of the contract having not been deposited at the time of filing the suit was not maintainable and the High court Division rightly affirmed the decree of the trial Court rejecting the plaint. 

 9. On perusal of the plaint as referred to by Mr. Abdul Haque we find that in paragraph 7 thereof, it has been categorically stated that the plaintiff made the balance amount of consideration of the contract pursuant to the deed of agreement. Whether the plaintiff made the payment(s) or not as asserted in the plaint is a question of fact which can only be decided or thrashed out at the trial of the suit considering the evidence. Therefore, when the plaintiff asserted that he paid the balance amount of the consideration of the contract and that there was no outstanding on the date when the suit was filed, there was no requirement of depositing the balance amount of consideration of the contract to file a suit for specific performance of contract.
